Plan: features from Chrome 130 to 160 combined with HTML-in-canvas

Every feature that chromestatus.com lists for Chrome 130 to 160, with a note on how it combines with a canvas that draws live DOM, and the demos built from those notes. Where a short test could settle a question it was run; those rows are marked measured, and the tests are on the probes page.

    Demos built from this plan

    In rank order. Every entry links directly to the live experiment page, plus what it shows, what was measured and which Chrome features it combines.

    What the probes found

    ProbeDetail

    Features by area

    The number is the first Chrome milestone with the feature on by default, or the first milestone of its trial. A blue bar marks rating 3: the feature changes what a canvas draws, or gives a drawn element a new input or output.

    Findings

    • CSS that changes an element's outline or paint is applied in the element picture: corner-shape, border-shape, clip-path: shape(), gap decorations, text-fit, caret-shape and custom highlights were all measured.
    • Scroll-driven animations and scroll-state() queries inside a drawn element raise the canvas's paint event with no script. streamAppendHTML() raises one paint event per chunk.
    • ::scroll-marker and ::scroll-button() pseudo-elements of a scroller in a canvas are drawn, and a real click on a drawn marker scrolls the list.
    • In Chromium 157 the browser tracks where an element is drawn: an element outside the canvas that is anchored to a canvas child follows the drawn position, an interestfor hint opens on hover at the drawn position, and highlightsFromPoint() and OpaqueRange rects use it. In Chromium 153 all four use the layout box.
    • A popover that is a descendant of a drawn element is not in its picture. It is shown in the top layer and hit tested there.
    • A float16 Display P3 canvas keeps a drawn element's wide-gamut colours and values above 1.0 (1.82 read back for an input of 4.0).
    • The browser protects two things from the canvas. Links are drawn as unvisited while the screen shows the :visited colour. Permission elements such as <geolocation> are drawn, and report isValid false with the reason intersection_occluded_or_distorted.
    • Not measured here: anything that needs a GPU, a headset, a sensor, a peripheral, an on-device model or a permission prompt. Those demos are in the hardware tier or name the requirement.

    The same content as one document: /chrome-apis/plan.md. To change an idea, edit tools/chrome-apis/ideas.json and run npm run build.
